articles.title_zh: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
facts_zh:
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
- Published
Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark trial in the US, AP reports.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.

all_titles.en: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering

The fate of the plane and its crew remained uncertain, it added.

articles.title_zh: Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight
facts_zh:
Indian government has 'lost the plot', says 'cockroach' leader barred from UK flight
- Published
One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.
Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.

In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people.

articles.title_zh: Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
facts_zh:
Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
- Published
A Zimbabwean national has been convicted by a court in South Africa of planning to go to fight in Ukraine.
The country has strict laws which restrict unauthorised involvement in overseas wars.
Twenty-four-year-old Wesley Sothole, who pleaded guilty, was handed a five-year suspended prison sentence and was ordered to be deported from South Africa.

French ex-President Sarkozy and wife Carla Bruni to face trial
- Published
Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.
The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.
The pair deny any wrongdoing.

articles.title_zh: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
facts_zh:
Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
- Published
At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.
Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said.
The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces.

articles.title_zh: Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war
facts_zh:
Land mine casualties soar in Syria, two years after war
- Published
Eleven-year-old Alaa was tending her family's goats with her siblings in a field behind their home in Umm Khuzaym, north-west Syria, on Sunday when there was a flash and a deafening bang.
"Then we heard people screaming," Alaa's father, Walid Mohammed Al-Ghafar, told the BBC.
Walid ran outside to find his daughter lying face down, killed, and her 10-year-old brother, Mahmoud, seriously injured.

articles.title_zh: Russian governor detained in rare criminal case against regional leader
facts_zh:
Russian governor detained in rare criminal case against regional leader
- Published
The governor of Russia's northern Murmansk region has been arrested on corruption charges in the first detention of a regional leader for five years.

Andrei Chibis, 47, is suspected of embezzlement and misappropriation of more than a billion roubles ($12.2.m; £9.3m) set aside to build an Arctic highway, as well as a further 39m roubles from the Murmansk construction budget.
Chibis is reported to have been detained as he arrived on a visit to Moscow on Monday and was taken in for questioning.

all_titles.en: Russian governor detained in rare criminal case against regional leader

Car bomb tears through Colombian city wounding more than 20
- Published
A car bomb has exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring at least 23 people.
The explosive device was detonated in front of the offices of the regional government, in the city centre, damaging several buildings.
No group has so far admitted carrying out the attack - the latest in a series using explosives to target official buildings and security forces' headquarters.

articles.title_original: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
articles.title_zh: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
facts_zh:
Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times
- Published
Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary.

In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.
"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions.

all_titles.en: Pope Francis' diary reveals claims he saw the devil three times

facts_zh:
Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
- Published
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media.
It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
